newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie dlr struggles to hold above US$0.74.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie dlr struggles to hold above US$0.74.

text.p: *Australian dollar vulnerable to retest of support under US$0.7400 after Thursday's wage data revives talk of rate cut.
*Break of US$0.7500, which would be a sign of renewed strength, now seen as unlikely in near term.
*Dollar follows U.S. dollar up against yen as regional currency concerns weigh on yen.
The Australian dollar was under pressure above US$0.7400 as it continued to unwind some of the week's gains on renewed talk of a sixth interest rate cut.
While the rate cut talk dominated, commodities also weakened with the CRB Index falling 2.34 points overnight, helping keep the dollar's bias to the downside.
The renewed pressure means a break of US$0.75, which would have been seen as bullish after a five month downtrend, is now not likely in the near term, traders said.
By 8.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) the Australian dollar was at US$0.7409/14, down on Thursday's late US$0.7436/41.
While the dollar has given up over half a cent from Thursday's high of US$0.7483, it is still up over one cent on last Friday's two year lows of US$0.7295.
With the rate talk capping the dollar, traders said the dollar was comfortable in a broad US$0.73/75 range, and it would take something unexpected to produce a break of that band.

Apart from some minor indicators, there is little local data of interest to the market until the end of August, which traders said would leave attention focused on rate differentials until next week's U.S. FOMC meeting, and leave the Aussie in the range it has traded since early July.

While down against the U.S. dollar, the Australian dollar had rallied against the yen on concerns that recent South East Asian currency instability may force Japan to weaken the yen to retain competitiveness in regional export markets.

Indonesia announced an effective float of the rupiah on Thursday, following similar action by some other South East Asian countries in recent weeks, and the U.S. dollar rose by about two yen to 118 yen.
The Australian dollar opened at 87.39/49 yen, up on Thursday's late 86.35/45.
